alerts.reason: Sales fell 19.7% from June to September, from $124.0 million to $99.6 million, while the corresponding 2020 quarters were nearly flat at $62.6 million and $62.7 million. September's 58.7% year-over-year gain leaves room for December to stay above -5%, but a sustained decline of this size could produce a March crossing as the Ariix combination enters the year-earlier comparison. Record C identifies the combination but gives no closing date, so the timing is uncertain.

September sales fell 4.58% year over year, just 0.42 percentage points above the threshold (A). Pricing gains could keep December above it (D). Chassis and component shortages were already reducing truck production and deliveries (C), so even a modest further loss of shipments could take March to a decline of at least 5%.

Sales fell from $123.2 million in June to $117.2 million in September as year-over-year growth slowed from 56.8% to 3.1%. Electrical demand and new industrial business supported September sales (A) and could keep December above -5%. Decreased demand across many regions (B) puts March at risk as the benefit of comparison with pandemic-depressed electrical demand fades.

Year-over-year sales growth slowed from 30.4% in June to 3.9% in September, with consolidated sales slipping from $279.1 million to $272.0 million (A). North American plant supply and labor constraints were already reducing sales in China and Japan (C). September's growth leaves room for December to remain above -5%, while further shipment losses could take March across it.

Record A's rounded nine-month increase of $7.2 billion, or 114%, and the supplied June and September sales imply roughly $5.0 billion of March 2021 revenue. A 5% March decline would therefore require revenue of about $4.7 billion or less. September revenue was already $3.84 billion, down from $4.68 billion in June despite 55% growth in subscription and services revenue (B). September's 26.7% total growth supports a December result above -5% before the much higher March comparison.

Revenue growth held near 1.5% in both June and September (A), supporting a December result above -5%. By September, deferred maintenance and support revenue had fallen $316.1 million since year-end, exceeding the $193.8 million increase in deferred subscription revenue (C). As customers shift from perpetual licenses to cloud services (D), that shortfall raises the risk of a March revenue decline of at least 5%.

Quarterly revenue edged up from $96.8 million to $98.1 million, yet year-over-year growth fell from 28.7% to 7.5% as the comparison rose from $75.2 million to $91.2 million. Multi-year OEM engagements provide some near-term revenue visibility (B), supporting December above -5%. If revenue stays near $98 million, a March 2021 comparison above roughly $103.2 million would produce a March 2022 crossing. The supplied records leave that comparison uncertain.

The year-over-year decline narrowed from 5.36% in June to 2.32% in September, supporting a December result above -5%. September revenue nevertheless fell to $109.7 million from $124.0 million in June. At September's year-over-year rate, a further 2.69 percentage points of weakness would trigger a fresh crossing. The timing of paid advertising and promotions can shift revenue between quarters (A).
